subject: A surveyed plot of square markers laid out frequency by time, where a vertical strip at the focus is surveyed sharp (bright solid markers, crisp hits) and the rest of the ground is smeared into even, hollow, mid-size markers.
controls: focus: position. The two strip boundary lines (1.5 px, past the neat line) and the solid bright markers between them slide across the plan, 100 Hz to 8 kHz, about 330 px.
tilt: scale. Marker size ramps across the plan from low to high frequency: at −6 the low side swells and the high side shrinks to 4 px, +6 the reverse (each marker 4–14 px).

blur: scale over time. Outside the strip each column's markers even out down the time axis: at 0 every column has the strip's crisp pattern (big at the three hits, tiny between), at 100 every row is the same mid size, the hits smeared away.
mix: count. A seeded scatter of markers outside the strip swaps between the dry look (the crisp pattern) and the wet look (smeared); mix sets how many have swapped, 0 to all 160.
reference: library/toro-blocks/contact.png (P10: a field computed from the signal model) beside opxy/reference/field-and-figure.jpg (neat ground, one figure)
risks: At 1:1 it reads as a matrix of LEDs or graph paper: a regular grid of identical squares is close to the 'dashboard of meters' the subject gate rejects.

Tilt and blur both change marker size (one across frequency, one down time); two controls on the scale channel of the same parts breaks the one-channel-per-control rule unless blur moves to shape (stretching markers into streaks along time) instead.
Size differences inside the haze are small at the default; the field looks uniform outside the strip, which is right for the sound but dull.
192 markers is fine for the node budget, but tilt and blur each resize nearly all of them: a turn redraws ~160 nodes, well past ~20 per frame while easing.
